title: Airflow in the data hall
alt: A face-on section across two rows in the data hall. On the left a rack faces a cold aisle; its back faces an enclosed hot aisle with a roof and an end door; on the right an in-row cooler sits in the next row. Cold air, drawn as blue dashed lines, comes from the in-row coolers into the rack fronts, turns red as the servers warm it, leaves the rack backs into the enclosed hot aisle and is pulled into the back of the in-row cooler. In the cooler a coil of chilled water takes the heat; chilled water comes in in a round blue pipe and warm water leaves in a round red pipe, on its way to be cooled again.
sources: Rack inlet air 18 to 27 degrees C recommended: ASHRAE Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments, 5th edition, reference card (figure only)
In-row cooler about 74 kW: Vertiv Liebert CRV CR050RC, 73.7 kW per unit (maker figure)
Chilled water supply at least 13 degrees C, return about 18 degrees C for an air-cooled hall: NREL / US DOE FEMP 2024
drawn_generically: a cut across one row pair: the left row is cut through a rack, the right row through an in-row cooler (the coolers sit between racks along each row); the cold air on the left is drawn coming from the next cooler along the row
rack, cooler, coil, hot-aisle roof and door: generic shapes
no hot-aisle temperature: the shared figures list has none
warm water out of the cooler is drawn red (water to be cooled), not violet: in this piece the heat is not reused
camera: the row pair, then close views of the rack, the hot aisle and the cooler, then the row pair

steps.caption: This is a cut across two rows in the data hall. The racks on the left face a cold aisle; their backs face an enclosed hot aisle. On the right is an in-row cooler, one of the cabinets that sit between the racks.
In-row coolers blow cold air into the cold aisles, in front of the racks.
Server fans pull the cold air in at the front of the rack. The servers warm it, and it leaves at the back.
The hot air is trapped in the enclosed hot aisle, so it cannot mix with the cold. The in-row cooler pulls it in at its back.
Inside the cooler, a coil of chilled water takes the heat out of the air. The air goes back out cold, and the water leaves warmer, on its way to be cooled again.
The whole loop: cold air in, through the servers, hot air out, back to the cooler, round again.
